description: Sets a property or calls a method on a node, or on one of the engine singletons nodePath names, in the running game. Needs the game running with the runtime addon. The answer carries elapsed_usec, how long the call or the write took inside the game, measured around it there: the round trip to the game is a second or more, so timing from outside measures that instead. A method that awaits is answered with the value it returns once it ends, and awaited true; elapsed_usec then runs to its end, and one that outlasts timeout is collected with op result. Errors the engine reported while a called method ran come back under errors and warnings under warnings, the first 20 of each, with errors_not_shown and warnings_not_shown counting the rest. A script error ends the function it is raised in, which then returns the default of its return type, 0, "" or null, so one that ended the called method itself is named under ended_by_error_at, and result is not a value the method returned. A call that takes longer than timeoutMs is not cancelled: the answer is pending: true with a requestId, the call goes on and does everything it was asked, and op result with that requestId collects its reply once it comes. A game this server started that its debugger holds is said so, with where, before a call and under heldAt when a call reached a breakpoint. Operations: set (needs nodePath, property, value): set a property, on a node or on an object it holds; call (needs nodePath, method): call a method, on a node or on an object it holds, and return its result; result (needs requestId): collect the reply to a set or call whose wait ran out, by the requestId it answered with.

args.description: call: the arguments, fitted to the method's parameter types. An RID is passed as the {"_type": "RID", "id": ...} a read answers it with, such as a viewport's for RenderingServer's render timing. A whole number of 2^53 or more, such as a 64-bit seed or a resource uid, is written as its digits, {"_type": "int", "value": "9007199254740993"}, the form a read answers with: a JSON number that large can arrive as a neighbour of the one sent, so sent as a number it is refused. A number a parameter would have to cut is refused rather than truncated: a fraction for an int, a number other than 0 or 1 for a bool. A vector, colour or the like may be written as its fields, {"x": 140, "y": 300}, or tagged, {"_type": "Vector2", "x": 140, "y": 300}. A parameter typed as an object takes a path naming one the game holds and is handed that instance: a colon path read from nodePath, "_game:run:wares:3", or one starting at a node, "/root/Main/Hud" or "/root/Main:_game:run". A path that reaches no object, or an object of another class than the parameter declares, is refused, and so are too few or too many arguments. The engine names a parameter typed as a script class without class_name by the class the script extends, so an object of that class with another script passes that check and the engine refuses the call: the answer says the method did not run, with the engine's reason. A parameter typed as a list or map, such as Array[int] or Array[Gear], is built from a JSON list or object element by element, objects named by their paths. The method itself takes its arguments here only: brackets on it holding arguments are refused. Only for op call.

method.description: call: which one to call. Colons call through what a node holds, "_game:run:advance", the same way a property is written through them, a list or a map is stepped into by index or key, "_game:run:roster:0:retire", and a step written as a call walks through what a reading method returned, "get_viewport():gui_get_focus_owner", as runtime_inspect property describes. Only for op call.

nodePath.description: Absolute node path, such as "/root/Main/Player", or the name of an engine singleton: Engine, Performance, RenderingServer, AudioServer, PhysicsServer2D, PhysicsServer3D, NavigationServer2D, NavigationServer3D, Time or TranslationServer, so "RenderingServer" with method viewport_get_measured_render_time_cpu reads what the engine measures. The other singletons are refused: OS runs programs, DisplayServer switches the keyboard layout and Input moves the real pointer. Only for ops set, call.

pid.description: Which game, when several are running from one project, such as a bench and its workers: its process id, as editor_status lists under runtimes. Without it the game this server started or plays is the one asked when it is among them, and the answer says so under answeredBy; with one game per project it is not needed at all.

projectPath.description: Which game, when more than one is running: the project directory it was started from. The pick without it, in order: the game this server started or is playing when it is among those running, named under answeredBy where there was a choice; else the only game there is; else a refusal naming every game and which argument tells them apart, pid when they are all one project and projectPath when they are not. Not needed with one game, nor for a call to this server's own.

properties.description: call: read the object the call answered with in the same answer, under result_properties: true for every variable its script declares, or a list of names, each a colon path walked from that object the way property paths are ("dead_allowed", "terms:0:name"). A name that is not there is listed under result_properties_missing with why, and a result that is not an object answers properties_note instead. Without it an object comes back as its class and id only. Only for op call.

property.description: set: which one to write. Colons write through what a node holds, "_game:run:day", and a number or a key steps into a list or a map on the way, "_game:run:roster:0:name", a negative number counting from the end, and a step written as a call, "get_viewport():gui_embed_subwindows", walks through what a reading method returned, as runtime_inspect property describes. A map keyed by numbers is stepped into by the number, "_game:units:3". A component of a vector, a colour or a transform, "position:x", writes that one alone: the value holding it is a copy, so it is put back where it was read from, setter and all, and a component of what a call returned is refused, since the game keeps that copy nowhere. The answer reads back off the same holder, and a write that leaves the property as it was is refused and says what it still holds: the engine not taking it and a setter keeping the value look the same, so the refusal names neither. A write of the value the property already holds, at its own precision, as a float given in 64 bits to a property keeping 32, is not refused: it answers unchanged: true. Only for op set.

requestId.description: result: the requestId a pending answer gave. Only for op result.

timeoutMs.description: set, call: how long to wait for the answer before answering pending with a requestId, which does not stop the call. Default 10000, or GDHARNESS_RUNTIME_TIMEOUT_MS. Give a longer one for a call known to take a while, such as one that plays many turns in one go. Only for ops set, call.

value.description: set: the value, fitted to the property's type. A whole number of 2^53 or more, such as a 64-bit seed or a resource uid, is written as its digits, {"_type": "int", "value": "9007199254740993"}, the form a read answers with: a JSON number that large can arrive as a neighbour of the one sent, so sent as a number it is refused. A number the property would have to cut is refused rather than truncated: a fraction into an int, a number other than 0 or 1 into a bool. A vector, colour or the like may be written as its fields, {"x": 140, "y": 300}, or tagged, {"_type": "Vector2", "x": 140, "y": 300}, which is the form a read answers with, and one carrying a field its type has not, such as a z for a Vector2, is refused naming it. A colour may also be given as its html code, "#ff8000" or "#ff800080". Text is written as sent: the JSON string "" writes an empty string, and quote marks inside the string are written into the text. An enum property takes the name of a value as well as its number, as the script or the inspector spells it, and a name none of its values has is refused listing them. A number past the range a property is exported with, or one none of its enum values has, is written, as the engine writes it, and the answer says so under outside_declared. A property typed as or holding an object takes a path naming one the game holds, the way call's args do, and holds that instance, or null, which the text null also means, to empty it. One declared as Variant or untyped takes anything, as the engine does: a value of the kind it holds is fitted to it, an int staying an int, and any other is stored as sent, a fraction into one holding an int included. A typed list or map, such as Array[int] or Dictionary[String, int], takes a JSON list or object with each element fitted to its element type, and an element that cannot become one is refused by its index or key, as is an object of another script than the one the list holds, whether or not that script has a class_name. Only for op set.

name: runtime_invoke
title: Set or call in the running game
